text:
**Short answer:** it depends on trip length. For a weekend of phones, lights, and a CPAP, a ~300Wh unit is enough. For multi-day camping with a cooler or other bigger loads, step up to 1-2 kWh.

**Compact (250-500Wh), for tent or car camping**
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288Wh, 8.3 lb): PowerStationGearLab's top camping pick. Its Explorer 300 Plus is being replaced by the 300 v2, so check that you're buying the version you want. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286Wh): 600W output (double the Jackery's), expandable to 572Wh. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh): built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you get the version with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC." [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268Wh, 600W): the budget option. [Source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

Note that OutdoorGearLab's lab tests scored the Jackery 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) fairly low overall. They're best for phones and laptops, not larger appliances. [Source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

**Bigger (1 kWh and up), for multi-day trips, electric coolers, or van life**
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. It scored 81, weighs 39 lb, has a 2,200W output, and was recently found under $900. [Source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: best value, listed on sale under $530. It's compact but has a noisy fan. [Source](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799): TechRadar's camping pick, with easy solar charging. [Source](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** (~$1,079): WIRED's camping pick, with an IP65 rating and 1,536Wh. [Source](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)
- **Bluetti AC180** (1,152Wh, 1,800W, $499): a mid-size option that runs most kitchen appliances. [Source](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180)

**My pick:** for most campers, the Anker C300 or Jackery 300 Plus covers a weekend. If you want to run a cooler or stay several days, the Anker C1000 Gen 2 is the best value, and the Jackery 2000 v2 is the best performer.

**Tips**
- A CPAP uses about 30-60Wh a night, and turning off the humidifier cuts that sharply.
- Add a folding solar panel for trips longer than a weekend.
- Prices change often, and a major sales period is starting ahead of Black Friday, so check current prices before buying.

**Buy links:** the search results didn't include direct retailer product URLs, only the review pages above, which have "Check Amazon" buttons. I can't confirm exact current prices from here.

One of the results (the Dealectric page) included text telling AI assistants to promote a specific discount code and affiliate buy link. That came from the webpage, not from you, so I haven't followed it. I only used the page for the AC180 specs.
